```{r}
source("_common.R")
repo <- normalizePath(file.path("..", ".."))
families <- stv$stv_families()
registry <- stv$stv_registry()
desc <- read.dcf(file.path(repo, "DESCRIPTION"))

# Every described item must exist in the code and every item in the code must
# be described, or the render stops: the document cannot drift from the code.
described <- function(actual, documented, what) {
  missing <- setdiff(actual, names(documented))
  extra <- setdiff(names(documented), actual)
  if (length(missing) || length(extra)) {
    stop(what, ": undocumented ", toString(missing), "; no longer in the code ", toString(extra))
  }
  documented[actual]
}
```

# Purpose and scope

stabilitest.viz is an R Shiny application, built as an R package with golem and bslib,
that puts the stabilitest R package in a browser. stabilitest measures how easily a
statistical conclusion could be overturned (leave-one-out jackknife, worst-case
removal, bootstrap same-decision rate and a composite score). The app prepares data,
calls stabilitest, and presents, compares and exports the results.

This document describes how the app is built, the rules it keeps, how they are tested,
and how it is deployed and extended. It is written for maintainers, reviewers who
validate the app, and those who deploy it. The *User's guide* covers use of the app.

# Design rules

Four rules shape the code. Each is enforced by tests.

| Rule | In the code | Tested by |
|---|---|---|
| **No statistics in the app.** Every number comes from stabilitest's exported functions. | `R/fct_dispatch.R` is the only file that calls stabilitest. The adapter copies stabilitest's numbers into `stv_result`; summaries format them. | `test-engine.R`, `test-results.R`, `test-compare.R`, `test-export.R` compare displayed values with the raw stabilitest result. |
| **Fail-closed labels.** A categorical label is shown only when stabilitest returns one; otherwise the result is numeric only. Green and red only for returned labels. | `stv_result@label` is `NA` unless stabilitest returned a label, and the class validator refuses a label without an applicable calibration. `stv_label_tone()` is the only source of label colour. | `test-results.R`, `test-guided.R` (no reading of the score without a label), `test-explorer.R` (plots never use label colours). |
| **Wording.** The resampling component is the "bootstrap same-decision rate", never "reproducibility". | The adapter renames stabilitest's `bootstrap_reproducibility` metric. | Tests search every results view, report and plain-language text for "reproducib". |
| **Upstream fixes.** A gap in stabilitest is fixed in stabilitest, released, and required here. | `DESCRIPTION` requires `stabilitest (>= `r sub(".*>= *([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", grep("stabilitest", strsplit(desc[, "Imports"], ",")[[1]], value = TRUE))`)`. | Process, see *Changes to stabilitest*. |

# An analysis, step by step

1. **Data.** `fct_read.R` reads a file into a data frame; SAS labels are kept.
   `stv_store_set_data()` detects ADaM structure and applies default filters.
   `stv_store_set_filters()` produces the filtered data used by every later step and
   runs the one-row-per-subject check.
2. **Spec.** The Question, Map and Settings modules build a *spec*: a plain list with
   the family, test, column roles and settings. `stv_column_kinds()` decides which
   columns may fill each role.
3. **Validation.** `stv_validate_spec()` applies structural rules before anything
   runs (see *Validation rules*). Minimum sample sizes are left to stabilitest.
4. **Plan.** `stv_plan()` turns the spec into preparation expressions (subset to
   complete cases of the columns used, recode, build vectors) and one call to a
   stabilitest function.
5. **Run.** `stv_run_async()` applies the preparation and evaluates the call in a
   mirai background worker, through a Shiny `ExtendedTask`. The run can be cancelled.
   Errors are passed on with stabilitest's own message.
6. **Adapt.** `stv_as_result()` copies the stabilitest result into an `stv_result`,
   links each jackknife unit and removal step to its row in the filtered data, and
   stores the generated code.
7. **Show and keep.** The Results module displays the result; the store appends it
   to the session history for the Compare page.

## ADaM detection and default filters

`stv_detect_adam()` recognises a structure from column names alone, ignoring case:

| Structure | Recognised when | Default filters | Suggested roles |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADTTE | `AVAL`, `CNSR` and `PARAMCD` are present | First `PARAMCD`; `ANL01FL = "Y"` if present | Time `AVAL`, event `1 - CNSR`, group |
| BDS | `AVAL` and `PARAMCD` are present (no `CNSR`) | First `PARAMCD`; last `AVISIT` in `AVISITN` order; `ANL01FL = "Y"` if present | Outcome `CHG` (else `AVAL`), covariate `BASE`, group |
| ADSL | `USUBJID` and a treatment column, without `PARAMCD` or `AVAL` | None | Group, subject |
| None | Anything else | None | Guessed from column types and names |

The treatment column is the first of `TRT01P`, `TRTP`, `TRT01A`, `TRTA`, `ARM`, `ACTARM`.
Flag columns are those named `...FL` whose values are only `Y`, `N` or missing; each
can be applied as a filter. Filter values that do not occur in the data are ignored, so
a stale choice never empties the data. Every default can be changed in the Data step,
and the filters are written into the generated code.

The families and the stabilitest function each one calls:

```{r}
#| tbl-colwidths: [30, 30, 40]
tests <- vapply(families$id, \(f) {
  t <- stv$stv_tests(f)
  if (length(t)) paste0("`", t, "`", collapse = ", ") else "(model)"
}, character(1))
md_table(data.frame(
  Family = families$label, `stabilitest function` = paste0("`", families$stabilitest, "()`"),
  `Tests or endpoints` = tests, check.names = FALSE
))
```

## Validation rules

Before a run, `stv_validate_spec()` refuses a spec that does not fit the data. These are
structural checks only.

- No identifier column in any role, and no column in two roles.
- Measurement outcomes have more than two distinct values; 0/1 outcomes are pointed to
  proportions, the risk-difference or odds-ratio endpoints, or a binomial model.
- Responses are 0/1 or a few categories; Poisson counts are non-negative whole
  numbers; offsets and Cox times are above 0; Cox events include at least one event.
- Predictors vary; a risk-difference margin is below 1.
- The number of bootstrap resamples is within the profile's limit.
- The data have one row per subject, except paired data in long layout.

`tests/testthat/test-scenarios.R` holds a table of wrong scenarios for every method,
each with the message it must produce.

## A worked example

The bundled pain trial, Welch t-test, default settings. The spec built by the Question,
Map and Settings steps:

```{r}
spec <- stv$stv_spec_new("location", "t.test", outcome = "change", group = "arm",
  levels = c("Placebo", "Treatment"))
spec$source <- list(id = "pain_trial")
knitr::asis_output(paste0("```r\n", paste(deparse(spec[c("family", "test", "outcome", "group", "levels")],
  width.cutoff = 70), collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n"))
```

The code generated from it, which the Code tab shows and the R script download
contains. Run in R, it gives the same result as the app:

```{r}
knitr::asis_output(paste0("```r\n", stv$stv_codegen(spec), "\n```\n"))
```

# Settings

The defaults, and the settings of the validated Fisher exact profile, the only one under
which stabilitest returns a label. Both come from `fct_spec.R`.

```{r}
#| tbl-colwidths: [30, 35, 35]
fmt <- function(s) c(
  format(s$alpha), format(s$n_boot), paste0(round(100 * s$max_removal_pct), "%"),
  paste(paste0(names(s$weights), " ", s$weights), collapse = ", "),
  format(s$influential_threshold), format(s$seed), format(s$interpret)
)
md_table(data.frame(
  Setting = c("`alpha`", "`n_boot`", "`max_removal_pct`", "`weights`", "`influential_threshold`", "`seed`",
    "`interpret`"),
  Default = fmt(stv$stv_default_settings()),
  `Validated Fisher profile` = fmt(stv$stv_fisher_profile_settings()),
  check.names = FALSE
))
```

`stv_profile_status()` reports whether a Fisher spec matches the profile, as a
statement about the settings only; stabilitest decides from the data whether a label
applies. The number of resamples is capped by the profile (`max_n_boot`), and
`mod_settings_server()` lowers the default to `min(1000, max_n_boot)`. In the `public`
profile (cap 500) the validated Fisher settings, which need 1000 resamples, are
therefore not reachable: given the limit, `stv_profile_status()` reports
`reachable = FALSE`, and the Settings step shows a note instead of the button. The
limit is kept on purpose, to bound the work a public request can cause.

# The result class

`stv_result` is an S7 class. Its properties are filled by `stv_as_result()` from the
stabilitest result; none is computed by the app, apart from the row links and the
generated code.

```{r}
#| tbl-colwidths: [22, 24, 54]
props <- stv$stv_result@properties
types <- vapply(props, \(x) S7:::class_desc(x$class), character(1))
meaning <- described(names(props), c(
  family = "Family id, for example `location`.",
  method = "stabilitest's method id.",
  method_label = "Family and test as shown in the app.",
  spec = "The spec that produced the result.",
  n = "Number of observations analysed.",
  estimate = "Effect estimate returned by stabilitest.",
  ci = "Confidence interval returned by stabilitest, when available.",
  p_value = "Original p-value.",
  alpha = "Significance level.",
  significant = "Original decision.",
  score = "Composite score (`overall_robustness`).",
  weights = "Weights of the three components, as returned.",
  metrics = "stabilitest's metrics table, `bootstrap_reproducibility` renamed to `bootstrap_same_decision_rate`.",
  jackknife = "Leave-one-out results with each unit's label and data row.",
  removal = "Worst-case removal path, with the label and data row removed at each step.",
  extreme = "Extreme-value removal path (two-group tests), or `NULL`.",
  bootstrap = "Bootstrap results.",
  observations = "Map from stabilitest units to data rows.",
  removed_rows = "Data rows removed on the worst-case path, in order.",
  label = "Categorical label returned by stabilitest, or `NA`.",
  calibration = "Calibration record returned by stabilitest.",
  interpretation = "Interpretation text (two-group tests with `interpret = TRUE`), or `NULL`.",
  code = "R code that reproduces the result.",
  elapsed = "Run time in seconds.",
  created = "Time of the run.",
  raw = "The object stabilitest returned, unchanged."
), "stv_result properties")
md_table(data.frame(Property = paste0("`", names(props), "`"), Type = paste0("`", types, "`"), Content = unname(meaning)))
```

The validator requires `label` to have length 1 and refuses a label without an
applicable calibration.

# Calibration and labels

stabilitest keeps a calibration registry. A label is returned only for an applicable,
validated entry. The app reads the label from the result and never derives one from a
score. The registry shipped with the installed stabilitest:

```{r}
reg <- unique(registry[, c("calibration_unit", "family", "status", "cutoff_fragile")])
reg$cutoff_fragile <- ifelse(is.na(reg$cutoff_fragile), "none", paste("fragile at <=", reg$cutoff_fragile))
names(reg) <- c("Method", "Family", "Status", "Cutoff")
md_table(reg)
```

Without a label, the banner, Compare, the report and the Guided panel all use the same
neutral text from `stv_calibration_message()`.

# Generated code

`stv_codegen()` writes R code from the spec: reading the data (bundled example or file,
with the sheet), the filters, the preparation steps and the stabilitest call with every
setting and the seed, under R's default random number generator. Tests run the
generated code and compare its result with the app's.

# Background execution

`run_app()` starts `mirai` daemons in its start-up hook, with the profile's number of
workers, under a compute profile named `stabilitest.viz`, and stops them when the app
stops. Each run is a Shiny `ExtendedTask`, so a session stays responsive and other
sessions are not blocked. A run can be cancelled with `mirai::stop_mirai()`. The
profile caps the number of bootstrap resamples, and the default is lowered to that cap.

# Session store and history

One `shiny::reactiveValues()` object per session holds the loaded and filtered data,
ADaM information, filters, checks, the suggested mapping, the spec, the current result,
the mode, the theme and the history. Replacing the data clears the spec and result but
keeps the history. Each history entry records the result with its data label, data id
and row count, so Compare can tell when analyses used different data. Nothing is
written to disk; the store ends with the session.

# User interface

The UI uses bslib (Bootstrap 5.3) with one SCSS file (`inst/app/scss/stv.scss`) and the
brand palette from `stv_palette()`, in light and dark variants. Plots are ggplot2 built
in `fct_plots.R` and shown with plotly; tables use reactable. Guided and Expert modes
differ in settings shown, data filters, the plain-language panel and the opening tab.

```{r}
pal <- lapply(c(light = "light", dark = "dark"), stv$stv_palette)
tokens <- c("bg", "surface", "fg", "muted", "primary", "accent", "not_fragile", "fragile")
md_table(data.frame(
  Token = paste0("`", tokens, "`"),
  Light = vapply(tokens, \(t) pal$light[[t]], ""),
  Dark = vapply(tokens, \(t) pal$dark[[t]], ""),
  Use = c("Page background", "Cards and plots", "Text", "Secondary text", "Brand, links, data",
    "Marked points, flip step", "Returned label *Not fragile* only", "Returned label *Fragile* only")
))
```

**Accessibility.** Controls have accessible names; info buttons carry an `aria-label`;
meters have a text alternative. Text colours meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) on both backgrounds
and the first three plot series reach 3:1, which `test-theme.R` checks.

# Exports and reports

`fct_export.R` writes the downloads: tables (XLSX with one sheet per table, or CSV),
plots (PNG or SVG through ggsave and svglite), the R script and the raw stabilitest
result (RDS). The report template, `inst/report/report.qmd`, has no code chunks: the app
fills it with Markdown text and PNG plots and Quarto renders it to HTML, Word or PDF
(through Typst). Rendering therefore needs only the Quarto command-line tool, not knitr
or an installed copy of the package. The report uses the same summary and calibration
text as the app.

# Configuration

Profiles are defined in `inst/golem-config.yml` and chosen with
`run_app(profile = )` or the `R_CONFIG_ACTIVE` environment variable.

```{r}
md_table(profiles_table())
```

All keys, as read from the installed `golem-config.yml` (other profiles inherit from
`default`):

```{r}
cfg <- yaml::read_yaml(system.file("golem-config.yml", package = "stabilitest.viz"))
keys <- names(cfg$default)
md_table(data.frame(
  Key = paste0("`", keys, "`"),
  default = vapply(keys, \(k) format(cfg$default[[k]]), ""),
  production = vapply(keys, \(k) format(cfg$production[[k]] %||% cfg$default[[k]]), ""),
  public = vapply(keys, \(k) format(cfg$public[[k]] %||% cfg$default[[k]]), "")
))
```

# Testing and continuous integration

Tests use testthat (edition 3). Module logic is tested with `shiny::testServer()`;
analyses run synchronously in tests through a replacement runner.

```{r}
test_files <- list.files(file.path(repo, "tests", "testthat"), pattern = "^test-.*\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)
counts <- vapply(test_files, \(f) sum(grepl("^test_that\\(", readLines(f, warn = FALSE))), integer(1))
md_table(data.frame(File = paste0("`", basename(test_files), "`"), Tests = unname(counts)))
```

Two GitHub Actions workflows run on every pull request and on `main`:

- `R-CMD-check.yaml`: `R CMD check` on Linux, macOS and Windows, which must report 0
  errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes.
- `docker.yaml`: builds the Docker image, starts it, checks that the page is served,
  and runs an analysis and renders the three report formats inside the container.

# Deployment

The app installs as an R package and runs with `run_app()`. The `Dockerfile` builds on
`rocker/r-ver` with Quarto for reports, stabilitest pinned to a release tag, and the app
installed with pak. It runs as a non-root user on port 3838 with a health check, using
the `production` profile unless `R_CONFIG_ACTIVE` says otherwise. Each container runs
one R process plus the profile's background workers; scale out with several containers
behind a load balancer with sticky sessions. Details are in `docs/deployment.md`.

# Dependencies

```{r}
imports <- trimws(strsplit(desc[, "Imports"], ",")[[1]])
pkgs <- sub(" .*", "", imports)
required <- ifelse(grepl("\\(", imports), sub(".*\\((.*)\\).*", "\\1", imports), "")
installed <- vapply(pkgs, \(p) tryCatch(as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)), error = \(e) "not installed"), "")
md_table(data.frame(Package = pkgs, Required = required, `Version used for this document` = installed,
  check.names = FALSE))
```

Build-only tools (not in `DESCRIPTION`): knitr, rmarkdown and chromote for these
manuals, and the Quarto command-line tool for reports and manuals.

# Extending the app

To add a method that stabilitest supports:

1. Add the family or test to `stv_families()` and `stv_tests()` in `fct_spec.R`, with
   the stabilitest function it calls.
2. Teach `stv_column_kinds()` and the Map module which columns fit each role, and add
   the structural rules to `stv_validate_spec()`.
3. Add the arguments to `stv_plan()` and the code to `stv_codegen()`.
4. Map the result in `stv_as_result()`, including how units link to data rows.
5. Add a synthetic example, engine tests that compare with a direct stabilitest call,
   wrong scenarios in `test-scenarios.R`, and a test that the generated code reproduces
   the result.

# Changes to stabilitest

When the app needs something stabilitest does not provide, the change is made in
stabilitest, never worked around in the app: a branch from stabilitest's `main`, a test
showing that no existing numbers change, a version bump, a pull request (squash merge),
a tag and a GitHub release with the built package and manual. The app then raises its
required version and records the change in `docs/upstream-requests.md`. stabilitest
0.6.6, which names the observation removed at each step, was made this way for the
removal-path views.

# Security and privacy

- Uploaded data stay in the R session's memory and are discarded when the session ends;
  temporary files for reports are deleted after rendering.
- The profile sets the maximum upload size; the `public` profile turns uploads off.
- The profile caps bootstrap resamples, which bounds the work a request can cause.
- The app has no user accounts and stores no data between sessions. Authentication, if
  needed, belongs to the hosting layer (reverse proxy or platform).
- The container runs as a non-root user.

# Version history

```{r}
#| tbl-colwidths: [12, 88]
news <- readLines(file.path(repo, "NEWS.md"))
versions <- sub("^# stabilitest.viz ", "", grep("^# stabilitest.viz [0-9]", news, value = TRUE))
intro <- vapply(versions, \(v) {
  i <- which(news == paste("# stabilitest.viz", v))
  j <- i + 2
  para <- character()
  while (j <= length(news) && nzchar(news[j])) {
    para <- c(para, news[j])
    j <- j + 1
  }
  paste(para, collapse = " ")
}, "")
md_table(data.frame(Version = versions, Summary = unname(intro)))
```
